| **Assessed** | 2026-11-27 |

AGI raises productivity through familiar automation and augmentation, bringing wage polarisation and shifting skill demand but no collapse in overall labour demand. Expanded unemployment insurance, earned-income tax credits and retraining cushion workers.

## Social contract scores (draft)

| Promise | Score | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hard work pays | 3 | Labour demand holds, but wage polarisation and re-employment at lower wages make gains uneven, and an expanded EITC keeps work paying. |
| Affordable essentials |  | Not addressed: the extract says nothing on housing, food, energy or care costs. |
| Reliable safety net | 4 | UI is widened to replace most of a worker's prior wage for longer and to cover gig workers and freelancers, and the EITC reaches workers without dependents, both scaling automatically. |
| Responsive government |  | Not addressed: only panel scores for the policies' Democratic Voice; nothing on how politics works in the scenario. |
| Time for what matters |  | Not addressed: the extract says nothing on working time, family or community in this scenario. |

## Policies from the atlas

- **Unemployment Benefits** (`unemployment-benefits`): Expanded UI, which automatically adjusts in scale if disruption increases, is assumed in place.
- **Tax Credit Expansion** (`tax-credit-expansion`): An expanded EITC, which automatically adjusts in scale if disruption increases, is assumed in place.
- **Workforce Training and Reskilling Investment** (`workforce-training-and-reskilling-investment`): Employer-led retraining is part of the preemptive stabilizer package assumed in the scenario.
- **Fiscal Automatic Stabilizers** (`fiscal-automatic-stabilizers`): The stabilizers "automatically adjust in scale if disruption increases", with escalation triggered by prolonged unemployment spells and falling median wages.
